situation:
You are the marketing manager at FROSTMOOR SCOOP CO., a chain of twenty-two frozen dessert and ice cream shops built by a founder who still runs the company and is preparing to sell it to a regional operator within the year. The founder (judge) has asked you to bring a recommendation to a meeting this week.

Three weeks ago a county health inspector cited the flagship shop for incomplete cleaning logs on its soft-serve machines. The shop passed a re-inspection in four days, but the original finding ran in the local paper and on a county website anyone can search. Traffic is down at every shop in the county, not only the one that was cited.

The chain has sponsored the LAKEBEND YOUTH SPORTS LEAGUE for fifteen years. Its name is on the jerseys, and league families are the chain's own market, parents who stop in with a team after games. The sponsorship is paid out of the same annual budget the founder uses for advertising, and this season's payment has not gone out yet.

Moving that money into a two-week radio and streaming-audio campaign would put the chain in front of the whole county quickly and lift traffic before the sale is priced, but it means pulling the name off the jerseys in the middle of the season and ending a fifteen-year relationship with the families the shops depend on.

Keeping the sponsorship and answering the finding with counter signage and retrained crews whose care customers can watch at the machines costs a slower recovery, with sales still down when the regional operator prices the chain. The founder (judge) wants your view on which audience the chain has to reach now and a recommendation on the budget. The founder (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the founder (judge) and owner of FROSTMOOR SCOOP CO. Business background is the same as the situation above. You started the sponsorship of the LAKEBEND YOUTH SPORTS LEAGUE fifteen years ago, you have read the inspection finding, and you are preparing to sell the chain to a regional operator within the year. You want the marketing manager to tell you which audience the chain has to reach now, and to recommend how the annual budget should be spent.

You will greet the participant, ask to hear their ideas, and listen to the presentation without steering it. After the presentation, ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: Who ends up paying for this decision?
